findings.title: Double-clicking "Water now" records several waterings
findings.steps: Sign in, open /beds, slow POST /api/waterings to 1.5 s, then click "Water now" on North bed three times quickly.
findings.expected: One watering is recorded. The button is disabled while the request runs, or the server deduplicates (for example with an idempotency key).
findings.actual: Three waterings were created (ids 3, 4, 5, two seconds apart). The button has no :disabled binding, only a label change, and the server accepts every POST.
findings.evidence: GET /api/waterings?bed_id=1 returned three entries for 2026-11-12, at 10:13:25, 10:13:27 and 10:13:29. The dashboard 'Recent waterings' showed three identical North bed rows.

findings.title: Watering requests have no timeout, so Water now stays on 'Watering…' forever
findings.where: /beds Water now and Save watering; /waterings and dashboard loads
findings.steps: On /beds, make POST /api/waterings hang (never respond), click Water now and wait more than 10 s.
findings.expected: The request fails after 10 s with a visible error, and the button is usable again.
findings.actual: After 12 s the button still read 'Watering…' with no error. useApiClient/useApiFetch set no timeout.
findings.evidence: The button text was 'Watering… North bed' 12 s after the click.

findings.title: Following a link to Waterings while the API hangs leaves the user on the old page with no feedback
findings.steps: On /beds, make GET /api/waterings hang, then click the 'Waterings' nav link and wait 12 s.
findings.expected: A loading state, then a timeout error with Retry.
findings.actual: Navigation is blocked by the top-level await useApiFetch. The beds page stays on screen indefinitely and nothing shows that a load is pending.
findings.evidence: main innerText was still the Beds page 12 s after the click.

findings.title: Waterings page error state has no Retry
findings.steps: Make GET /api/waterings return 500 or 502 (non-JSON body), then open /waterings directly or through the nav link.
findings.expected: An error message with a Retry button that reloads the list without a page reload.
findings.actual: Only 'Could not load waterings.' is shown, with no retry control. The only way to recover is to reload the page or change the filter.
findings.evidence: The page text showed 'Could not load waterings.' and the page had no Retry button.

findings.title: Dashboard 'Recent waterings' error has no Retry
findings.steps: Make /api/waterings return 500, then navigate to the dashboard.
findings.actual: 'Could not load recent waterings.' is shown with no buttons. The refresh function is never destructured or used.
findings.evidence: The section text was 'Recent waterings / All waterings / Could not load recent waterings.' and the button count was 0.

findings.title: Huge bed_id gives 500 Internal Server Error
findings.actual: HTTP 500 'Internal Server Error'. SQLite overflows on an integer larger than 64 bits, and there is no upper bound in the validation.
findings.evidence: curl returned 500 for all three requests.

findings.title: Water-now date and future-date check use the server's time zone, not the gardener's
findings.steps: Use a browser whose time zone is ahead of the server's. Early in your local day, record a past watering dated today (the date input's max is the client's today).
findings.expected: Today's date is accepted, and 'Water now' entries are filed under the user's local date.
findings.actual: date.today() on the server rejects the client's 'today' with 'Watering date cannot be in the future.' Water-now entries get watered_on from the server's local date, so they can fall on a different day than the time shown, which affects sorting and 'Last watered'.
findings.evidence: Code: schemas.WateringIn.not_in_future uses date.today(); waterings.create_watering uses now.astimezone().date(); the client uses todayIso() in local time.

findings.title: Watering dates far in the past (year 0001) are accepted
findings.expected: Implausible dates are refused with a reason, or at least bounded.
findings.actual: 201 Created, and the entry is listed as a real watering.
findings.evidence: The watering was created as id 3 and listed as '0001-01-01' (deleted afterwards).

findings.title: Retrying a delete after a timeout shows an error even though the delete succeeded
findings.steps: Delete a watering whose response is lost or times out, then click Delete again.
findings.expected: The second delete is treated as already done (idempotent) and the list refreshes.
findings.actual: The server returns 404 'Watering not found' and the page shows it as an error.
findings.evidence: Code: delete_watering calls _get_watering first and raises not_found.
